q1.answer: Backstage decided that any fetch or XMLHttpRequest in tests must be mocked with msw (route-style handlers via setupServer/http.get) rather than mocking fetch directly, following react-testing-library's recommendation and to have one consistent request-mocking approach across test types. This exercises the client's real fetch path against a fake server, at the cost of a little more code.

q2.answer: ADR014 (Proper use of HTTP fetching libraries), which supersedes ADR013, says frontend plugins should prefer fetchApiRef, and injectable clients should accept a fetch implementation so callers can adorn calls with auth or other information and track metrics; it also moves away from third-party fetch packages like node-fetch. Injecting fetchApi from fetchApiRef in plugin.ts follows this.

q3.answer: Backstage standardized on Luxon as its single date library because Moment.js has large bundles and mutable state and is being sunset, while Luxon offers a similar API with immutability and native Intl, giving smaller bundles; native Date lacks features like relative formatting ('a day ago'). ADR012 additionally prefers Luxon's toLocaleString presets for locale-friendly display.

q4.answer: Backstage decided to avoid React.FC/React.SFC in new code, following create-react-app's removal of it, because FC implicitly adds a children prop and does not support generics well, with next to no benefit; components should type props directly (adding children explicitly if needed).

q5.answer: ADR004 requires every exported symbol to be traceable through index files up to src/index.ts, with each index re-exporting only its immediate children, so you can tell whether a symbol is public by walking index files toward the root; deep re-exports from the root would break that guarantee. Index-to-index re-exports use `export *`, while indexes over non-index files list exports explicitly.
